title: Book of Kells, Chi Rho page

source.author: Unknown Columban scribes/illuminators, c. 800; reproduction uploader not stated (PD-Art)
source.notes: Best colour reproduction of the Chi Rho page on Commons; only 1123 x 1558 px, below the 2000 px target. Every other Commons copy of fol. 34r is smaller (484 x 641 PNG) or a black-and-white lantern slide (KU Leuven GD017031, 3797 x 3230). A larger scan of a different full-page illumination (fol. 32v, 2202 x 2918, from Trinity College Dublin's digital collections) is listed as alternative 1. Trinity's own digital collection is not used because its image licence was not verified as free. Dates, size (33 x 25.5 cm), vellum and shelfmark from Wikidata Q204221 and en.wikipedia 'Book of Kells'; place of creation is uncertain (a Columban monastery in Ireland or Scotland), Iona chosen with coordinates from Wikidata Q610.

madeIn.name: Iona Abbey (or Kells), Columban monastery
madeIn.region: Inner Hebrides, Scotland (or County Meath, Ireland)

object.medium: Ink and pigments on calf vellum
object.description: The Chi Rho page opens the account of Christ's birth in Matthew's Gospel: the Greek letters Chi, Rho and Iota, the abbreviation of 'Christ', fill the page with spirals, interlace, animals and tiny human figures. The Book of Kells, a Latin Gospel book made in a Columban monastery around 800, is the most elaborately decorated of the Insular manuscripts. It has been at Trinity College Dublin since the seventeenth century. The page is folio 34r.
facts: The manuscript has 340 folios of calf vellum, each page about 33 by 25 cm, bound since 1953 in four volumes.
It contains ten full-page illustrations and was made in a Columban monastery in Ireland or Scotland around 800.
UNESCO added the Book of Kells to its Memory of the World Register in 2011.
